messages:
maria-cs: Customer (Blackbox) reports private service endpoints failing to resolve from their VPC after a config change. They see app errors: `dial tcp: lookup svc.internal.blackbox.com: no such host`. Customer says it worked yesterday.

alex-support: Thanks — can you paste the exact error and a couple quick repro steps the customer ran? Also which region & VPC id?

maria-cs: Error from their app pod logs: `rpc: dial tcp: lookup svc.internal.blackbox.com: no such host`. Repro steps they gave: (1) ssh to bastion in vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2), (2) `curl http://svc.internal.blackbox.com/health` -> curl: "Could not resolve host". They included dig output.

maria-cs: dig +short svc.internal.blackbox.com -> (empty)

maria-cs: dig @10.0.0.2 +short svc.internal.blackbox.com -> (empty)

maria-cs: dig @10.0.0.2 svc.internal.blackbox.com A +trace -> shows NXDOMAIN at final step

alex-support: OK. Two immediate suspects: 1) Route53 private hosted zone not associated with that VPC (classic cause), or 2) resolver rule/forwarder is misconfigured (split-horizon) or customer changed NACL/SG/firewall blocking DNS.

jamie-net: Can the customer run this quick check from the bastion?
```bash
# list hosted zones associated with the VPC
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c3d --vpc-region us-west-2
```

jamie-net: If the private zone `internal.blackbox.com` doesn't appear, it's not associated. If we host the private zone in our account, they need an association (or we need to create a delegation).

maria-cs: They ran the command and posted output: `[]` (empty).

tom-infra: That nails it — empty association. But two flavors: a) our private zone exists in our org account but not associated to their VPC, b) there's a same-name public zone overshadowing it (split-horizon). Route53 will prefer a private hosted zone for associated VPCs only. If the VPC isn't associated, you'll fall back to public resolution (which often NXDOMAIN).

route53-bot: Found private hosted zone `Z1ABCDXYZ` for `internal.blackbox.com` in account redwood-prod (us-west-2). Current VPC associations: vpc-0deadbeef (redwood infra), vpc-0fff1111 (redwood infra). Not associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d (customer).

alex-support: So cause = missing VPC association. Two safe remediation paths: (A) Create a cross-account VPC association to the private hosted zone pointing at customer's VPC (if policy allows), or (B) ask customer to create a CNAME to public endpoint or set up an outbound forwarder. Which we choose depends on contract and security.

maria-cs: Customer wants minimal changes on their side. They asked if we can associate the zone to their VPC from our account.

jamie-net: We can do a cross-account association but need their VPC ID and account ID. Also they must allow associate-hosted-zone permission from our account. Steps for us (in redwood-prod account):
```bash
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z1ABCDXYZ \
  --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d
```
# For cross-account, customer must approve via console or we need delegation policy (see AWS docs).
```

jamie-net: Also check resolver rules: if they have outbound forwarding rules that redirect `internal.blackbox.com` to a custom resolver, that can override. Run `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d`.

maria-cs: They ran the assoc list — nothing for `internal.blackbox.com`.

tom-infra: Another quick check: confirm nothing is blocking DNS at the network level. From bastion run:
```bash
# test UDP and TCP DNS reachability to AmazonProvidedDNS (base+2 = .2 in subnet)
dig @10.0.0.2 svc.internal.blackbox.com +time=2 +tries=1
# try TCP
dig @10.0.0.2 +tcp svc.internal.blackbox.com
# test from pod
kubectl run --rm -i --tty dns-debug --image=busybox --restart=Never -- sh -c "nslookup svc.internal.blackbox.com"
```

maria-cs: Customer ran the tcp/udp tests — both returned NXDOMAIN. NACLs and SGs show UDP/TCP 53 allowed to .2.

alex-support: So the network isn't blocking; the DNS server at .2 is returning NXDOMAIN because the zone isn't associated. Next step: confirm we can create the association. @jamie-net can you check org policies for cross-account associate-hosted-zone? Also check whether the private zone contains the records they need (A/ALIAS).

jamie-net: I checked. Policy allows us to associate, but then customer will need to accept or we need their account id. I'll prepare a quick checklist and an IAM snippet they can run to grant `route53:AssociateVPCWithHostedZone` for our principal.

maria-cs: Customer is OK to run a one-off CLI. I'll post the CLI and a minimal IR doc.

alex-support: For rollback/backout: if anything looks off after association, we can disassociate the VPC: `aws route53 disassociate-vpc-from-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z1ABCDXYZ --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d`. Also recommend they flush node/agent caches and restart kube-dns/coredns: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns`.

maria-cs: I've sent the CLI and instructions to the customer. They confirmed running the associate call (they gave us a screenshot of successful CLI).

route53-bot: VPC association event: hosted-zone Z1ABCDXYZ associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2) by 123456789012.

maria-cs: After association, customer reran `dig @10.0.0.2 +short svc.internal.blackbox.com` -> `10.10.10.45`

maria-cs: And their app `curl` now returns 200. Customer confirmed service is recovered. :tada:

alex-support: Great. Closing action items: jamie-net to add a one-pager on cross-account private zone associations to support runbook; tom-infra to add a check in onboarding to ensure hosted-zone association is validated for Private deployments.

jamie-net: I'll draft the runbook and include the `list-hosted-zones-by-vpc`, `list-resolver-rule-associations`, and sample `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` commands plus troubleshooting steps (dig tcp/udp, coredns restart).

tom-infra: I'll add a post-provision check that fails the infra health check if `dig` from a test instance returns NXDOMAIN for expected internal endpoints.

maria-cs: Customer happy, closing thread.

alex-support: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone."
